newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's PBR to issue up to 4.45 mln shrs.
newsitem.headline: Poland's PBR to issue up to 4.45 mln shrs.

text.p: Shareholders of Polish Development Bank SA (PBR) set its planned share issue, part of a scheme to join other banks in forming a group, at between one million and 4.45 million shares, PBR said on Friday.
The shareholders approved the management's plan that the ex-rights issue contain both a closed tranche for financial institutional investors and an open tranche, the bank said in a statement.
The statement said the closed tranche would hold up to 3.7 million shares and the open tranche up to one million. @
It said the price would not be lower than either PBR's average bourse price over the last three months or the share's book value on February 28 and that management would set a subscription period.
PBR currently has 14,072,600 shares outstanding and is 32.9-percent owned by Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), with the state treasury holding 29.5 percent.
PBR had previously said it would issue up to 8.4 million shares to attract strategic investors and help finance its participation in the group, linking four banks and an insurer.
PBK is to be privatised later this year and PBR has said it will seek 15 percent.

PBK announced earlier in the week that PBR, Bank Przemyslowo-Kredytowy (BPH), Kredyt Bank and insurer Warta had formed a consortium agreement to buy a stake of at least 50 percent plus one share in PBK.
The finance ministry plans to sell 65 percent of PBK to a foreign or domestic strategic investor by the end of April and follow it with a public offering of 15 percent around October.
PBR, PBK, BPH, Kredyt Bank and Warta have been taking cross holdings in one another under a scheme to create the group.
